title: ASL: Fingerspelling and 100 Core Signs
description: For beginners: 26 fingerspelled letters and 100 everyday ASL concepts in original text descriptions. Use your dominant hand unless stated; regional variants exist. Practice with fluent signers and visual demonstrations.

sources.name: ASL University: public sign reference

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter A.
cards.back: Make a fist with the thumb resting alongside the index finger, not across the fingers. Palm faces forward.
cards.example: Use A as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.
cards.hint: Compare the thumb position with S.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter B.
cards.back: Hold four fingers straight up and together, palm forward, with the thumb folded across the palm.
cards.example: Use B as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter C.
cards.back: Curve the fingers and thumb to outline the letter C; the opening faces sideways.
cards.example: Use C as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter D.
cards.back: Touch the thumb to the curved middle, ring, and little fingertips; point the index finger up. Palm faces forward.
cards.example: Use D as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter E.
cards.back: Bend all four fingers toward the palm so the fingertips approach or rest on the thumb. Palm faces forward.
cards.example: Use E as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter F.
cards.back: Touch index fingertip to thumb tip in a small circle; hold the other three fingers up. Palm faces forward.
cards.example: Use F as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter G.
cards.back: Point the index finger sideways with the thumb extended parallel below it; curl the other fingers. The palm faces toward your body.
cards.example: Use G as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter H.
cards.back: Extend index and middle fingers together sideways, with the other fingers folded. Palm faces toward your body.
cards.example: Use H as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter I.
cards.back: Make a fist with the little finger extended upward. Palm faces forward.
cards.example: Use I as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter J.
cards.back: Start with the I handshape and trace a small J in the air with the little fingertip, curving at the bottom.
cards.example: Use J as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter K.
cards.back: Extend the index and middle fingers in a V and place the thumb against the base of the middle finger. Palm faces forward.
cards.example: Use K as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter L.
cards.back: Extend index finger up and thumb sideways to form an L. Fold the other fingers; palm faces forward.
cards.example: Use L as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter M.
cards.back: Make a fist with the thumb tucked under the index, middle, and ring fingers so its tip appears between ring and little fingers.
cards.example: Use M as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter N.
cards.back: Make a fist with the thumb tucked under index and middle fingers so its tip appears between middle and ring fingers.
cards.example: Use N as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter O.
cards.back: Curve all fingers to meet the thumb and form a rounded O. Keep the opening visible from the side.
cards.example: Use O as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter P.
cards.back: Use the K handshape tilted downward, with the middle finger pointing down.
cards.example: Use P as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.
cards.hint: Start from K and change the orientation.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter Q.
cards.back: Use the G handshape tilted downward, with index finger and thumb pointing toward the floor.
cards.example: Use Q as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter R.
cards.back: Cross the middle finger over the index finger; fold the other fingers under the thumb. Palm faces forward.
cards.example: Use R as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter S.
cards.back: Make a fist with the thumb across the front of the fingers. Palm faces forward.
cards.example: Use S as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter T.
cards.back: Make a fist with the thumb tucked between the index and middle fingers, its tip visible.
cards.example: Use T as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter U.
cards.back: Extend index and middle fingers straight up together; fold other fingers under the thumb. Palm faces forward.
cards.example: Use U as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter V.
cards.back: Extend index and middle fingers upward and apart; fold other fingers under the thumb. Palm faces forward.
cards.example: Use V as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter W.
cards.back: Extend index, middle, and ring fingers upward, spread slightly; hold the little finger down with the thumb. Palm faces forward.
cards.example: Use W as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter X.
cards.back: Make a fist, then raise the index finger in a bent hook shape. Palm faces forward or slightly sideways.
cards.example: Use X as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter Y.
cards.back: Extend the thumb and little finger, folding the other three fingers. Palm faces forward.
cards.example: Use Y as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: Fingerspell the letter Z.
cards.back: Extend the index finger and trace a Z: across, diagonally down, then across again. Fold the other fingers.
cards.example: Use Z as one letter in a fingerspelled name; keep the hand in a comfortable signing space.

cards.front: How do you sign HELLO in ASL?
cards.back: Touch the fingertips of a flat dominant hand near the forehead, palm angled outward, then move the hand away in a small salute.
cards.example: Greet someone as you begin a conversation.

cards.front: How do you sign GOODBYE in ASL?
cards.back: Hold an open hand outward and bend the fingers down and up in a small wave.

cards.front: How do you sign PLEASE in ASL?
cards.back: Place a flat dominant hand on the upper chest and make a small circular motion.

cards.front: How do you sign THANK YOU in ASL?
cards.back: Touch the fingertips of a flat dominant hand near the chin, palm toward you, then move the hand forward toward the person.

cards.front: How do you sign SORRY in ASL?
cards.back: Make a dominant A hand or fist and circle it against the chest.

cards.front: How do you sign YES in ASL?
cards.back: Make a dominant S fist and move it up and down at the wrist, like a nod.

cards.front: How do you sign NO in ASL?
cards.back: Extend the index and middle fingers together above the thumb, then close them against the thumb.

cards.front: How do you sign HELP in ASL?
cards.back: Place the dominant A hand, thumb up, on the nondominant open palm and lift both hands. Direction can show who helps whom.

cards.front: How do you sign STOP in ASL?
cards.back: Hold the nondominant palm up. Bring the little-finger edge of a flat dominant hand down onto that palm.
cards.example: Ask for an action to cease.

cards.front: How do you sign FINISH in ASL?
cards.back: Hold both open hands near the torso with palms toward you, then flick or rotate them so palms face outward.
cards.example: Indicate that an activity is complete.

cards.front: How do you sign AGAIN in ASL?
cards.back: Hold the nondominant palm up. Arc a bent dominant hand down so its fingertips land on the palm.

cards.front: How do you sign MORE in ASL?
cards.back: Bring the fingertips and thumbs of each hand together into flattened O shapes, then tap the two sets of fingertips together.

cards.front: How do you sign WANT in ASL?
cards.back: Hold both open hands in front, palms up, and pull them toward yourself while curling the fingers slightly.

cards.front: How do you sign NEED in ASL?
cards.back: Point a bent dominant index finger forward and move it downward at the wrist.

cards.front: How do you sign LIKE in ASL?
cards.back: Touch the chest with the dominant thumb and middle finger apart, then draw them away while bringing them together.

cards.front: How do you sign LOVE in ASL?
cards.back: Cross both arms over the chest, with hands closed or loosely fisted.
cards.example: Express love for a person or activity.

cards.front: How do you sign GOOD in ASL?
cards.back: Move the fingertips of a flat dominant hand from the chin forward and down to the upturned nondominant palm.

cards.front: How do you sign BAD in ASL?
cards.back: Move the fingertips of a flat dominant hand from the chin outward while turning the palm downward.

cards.front: How do you sign HAPPY in ASL?
cards.back: Brush one or both open hands upward on the chest in repeated light movements.

cards.front: How do you sign SAD in ASL?
cards.back: Hold open hands in front of the face, palms toward you, then lower them with a sad facial expression.

cards.front: How do you sign ANGRY in ASL?
cards.back: Hold a clawed dominant hand near the lower face and move it outward slightly, using an angry expression.

cards.front: How do you sign TIRED in ASL?
cards.back: Place fingertips of bent hands near the upper chest; let both hands drop as the shoulders relax.

cards.front: How do you sign SICK in ASL?
cards.back: Touch the forehead with the bent middle finger of one hand and the abdomen with the bent middle finger of the other.

cards.front: How do you sign HUNGRY in ASL?
cards.back: Place a dominant C hand near the upper chest and draw it down along the torso.

cards.front: How do you sign THIRSTY in ASL?
cards.back: Move the dominant index finger downward along the front of the throat.

cards.front: How do you sign EAT in ASL?
cards.back: Bring the gathered fingertips of the dominant hand to the mouth in a small repeated motion. This handshape also appears in FOOD.

cards.front: How do you sign DRINK in ASL?
cards.back: Shape the dominant hand like a C-shaped cup and tip it toward the mouth as if drinking.
cards.example: Refer to drinking from a cup.

cards.front: How do you sign WATER in ASL?
cards.back: Tap the index-finger side of a dominant W hand near the chin.

cards.front: How do you sign MILK in ASL?
cards.back: Open and close a dominant hand in a squeezing motion, as if milking.
cards.example: Refer to milk as a beverage.

cards.front: How do you sign COFFEE in ASL?
cards.back: Stack two fists, one above the other, and circle the upper fist above the lower, like turning a grinder.

cards.front: How do you sign TEA in ASL?
cards.back: Hold the nondominant hand as a small cup; circle the dominant thumb and index pinch near or inside its opening.
cards.example: Refer to a cup of tea.

cards.front: How do you sign BREAD in ASL?
cards.back: Hold the nondominant hand upright as a loaf. Move the little-finger side of a dominant flat hand downward across its back twice, as if slicing.
cards.example: Ask for bread with a meal.

cards.front: How do you sign CHEESE in ASL?
cards.back: Press the palms together and twist or rock them against each other.
cards.example: Refer to cheese in a sandwich.

cards.front: How do you sign APPLE in ASL?
cards.back: Place the knuckle of a bent dominant index finger at the cheek and twist the hand.

cards.front: How do you sign BANANA in ASL?
cards.back: Hold the nondominant index finger upright. Use the dominant pinched fingers to mime peeling strips downward from it.

cards.front: How do you sign ORANGE in ASL?
cards.back: Open and close a dominant fist near the mouth, like squeezing. Context distinguishes the fruit and color.
cards.example: Describe an orange fruit or the color orange.

cards.front: How do you sign COOKIE in ASL?
cards.back: Hold the nondominant palm up. Place a curved dominant hand on it, lift slightly, rotate, and place it down again like a cookie cutter.

cards.front: How do you sign EGG in ASL?
cards.back: Hold two H hands facing each other with fingertips meeting, then turn them downward and apart as if cracking an egg.
cards.example: Refer to an egg for breakfast.

cards.front: How do you sign MEAT in ASL?
cards.back: Use the dominant thumb and index finger to grasp the fleshy area between the nondominant thumb and index finger and give it a small shake.
cards.example: Refer to meat in a meal.

cards.front: How do you sign GREEN in ASL?
cards.back: Hold a dominant G hand outward and shake or twist it gently at the wrist.

cards.front: How do you sign MOTHER in ASL?
cards.back: Spread all five fingers and touch the dominant thumb to the chin.

cards.front: How do you sign FATHER in ASL?
cards.back: Spread all five fingers and touch the dominant thumb to the forehead.

cards.front: How do you sign GRANDMOTHER in ASL?
cards.back: Start with the open-hand MOTHER position at the chin, then move the hand forward in two small arcs.

cards.front: How do you sign GRANDFATHER in ASL?
cards.back: Start with the open-hand FATHER position at the forehead, then move the hand forward in two small arcs.

cards.front: How do you sign BOY in ASL?
cards.back: Bring the dominant fingers and thumb together near the forehead as if grasping a cap brim.

cards.front: How do you sign GIRL in ASL?
cards.back: Brush the dominant thumb down the side of the cheek toward the chin, using an A-like handshape.

cards.front: How do you sign BABY in ASL?
cards.back: Cradle one forearm in the other and rock both arms as if holding a baby.

cards.front: How do you sign FRIEND in ASL?
cards.back: Hook the two index fingers together, then reverse which hand is on top and hook them again.

cards.front: How do you sign FAMILY in ASL?
cards.back: Use F handshapes on both hands, with thumb-index circles initially near each other and palms facing each other. Arc both hands outward and around until little-finger sides meet.
cards.example: Refer to your family as a group.

cards.front: How do you sign NAME in ASL?
cards.back: Extend index and middle fingers together on both hands. Tap the dominant pair crosswise on the nondominant pair.

cards.front: How do you sign DEAF in ASL?
cards.back: Touch the dominant index finger near the ear and then near the mouth; the reverse order also occurs.
cards.example: Describe a Deaf person or Deaf identity.

cards.front: How do you sign HEARING in ASL?
cards.back: Circle the dominant index finger forward near the mouth, with the finger pointing sideways.

cards.front: How do you sign I / ME in ASL?
cards.back: Point the dominant index finger toward your own chest.

cards.front: How do you sign YOU in ASL?
cards.back: Point the dominant index finger toward the person being addressed.

cards.front: How do you sign MY in ASL?
cards.back: Place the dominant flat palm on the chest.

cards.front: How do you sign YOUR in ASL?
cards.back: Direct a flat open palm toward the person addressed.
cards.example: Indicate something belongs to the other person.

cards.front: How do you sign WHO in ASL?
cards.back: Place the thumb of a dominant L-like hand near the chin and bend the extended index finger repeatedly; use a wh-question expression.

cards.front: How do you sign WHAT in ASL?
cards.back: Hold both open hands palm up and move them slightly side to side, with a questioning expression.

cards.front: How do you sign WHERE in ASL?
cards.back: Hold the dominant index finger upright and wag it side to side, with a wh-question expression.

cards.front: How do you sign WHEN in ASL?
cards.back: Hold the nondominant index finger upright. Circle the dominant index fingertip around it, then bring the fingertips together; use a questioning expression.

cards.front: How do you sign WHY in ASL?
cards.back: Touch dominant fingertips near the forehead, then draw the hand away into a Y handshape, with a questioning expression.

cards.front: How do you sign HOW in ASL?
cards.back: Bring the knuckles of bent hands together, then rotate the hands open so palms face up, with a questioning expression.
cards.example: Ask about a method or condition.

cards.front: How do you sign WHICH in ASL?
cards.back: Hold two A hands, thumbs up, and alternately raise them slightly, with a questioning expression.
cards.example: Ask someone to choose between options.

cards.front: How do you sign UNDERSTAND in ASL?
cards.back: Near the forehead, start with a loose fist and flick the index finger upward, like an idea appearing.

cards.front: How do you sign KNOW in ASL?
cards.back: Touch the fingertips of a flat dominant hand to the side of the forehead.

cards.front: How do you sign THINK in ASL?
cards.back: Touch the dominant index finger to the forehead.
cards.example: Refer to thinking or an opinion.

cards.front: How do you sign LEARN in ASL?
cards.back: Hold the nondominant palm up. Gather imaginary information from it with the dominant fingers and bring the gathered fingertips to the forehead.

cards.front: How do you sign TEACH in ASL?
cards.back: Hold both flattened O hands near the forehead, then move them forward together.

cards.front: How do you sign SCHOOL in ASL?
cards.back: Clap the dominant flat hand lightly on the upturned nondominant palm twice.

cards.front: How do you sign BOOK in ASL?
cards.back: Place both palms together with fingers pointing forward, then open the hands like a book while the little-finger sides stay together.

cards.front: How do you sign PAPER in ASL?
cards.back: Hold the nondominant palm up; brush or tap the heel of the dominant palm against it twice.
cards.example: Ask for a sheet of paper.

cards.front: How do you sign WRITE in ASL?
cards.back: Hold the nondominant palm up; mime writing on it with the dominant thumb and index finger pinched as if holding a pen.

cards.front: How do you sign READ in ASL?
cards.back: Hold the nondominant hand flat as a page. Point a dominant V hand toward it and move the fingertips down the page.

cards.front: How do you sign WORK in ASL?
cards.back: Hold both hands in S fists, palms down, and tap the dominant wrist area onto the back or wrist area of the nondominant fist.
cards.example: Refer to a job or work.

cards.front: How do you sign PLAY in ASL?
cards.back: Hold Y hands on both sides and shake or rotate them outward repeatedly.

cards.front: How do you sign WALK in ASL?
cards.back: Hold both flat hands palm down and alternate them forward, tipping them like feet taking steps.

cards.front: How do you sign SIT in ASL?
cards.back: Hold the nondominant index and middle fingers together horizontally. Place bent dominant index and middle fingers over them like seated legs.

cards.front: How do you sign STAND in ASL?
cards.back: Place the downward-pointing fingers of a dominant V hand on the upturned nondominant palm, like two standing legs.

cards.front: How do you sign SLEEP in ASL?
cards.back: Hold an open hand in front of the face and draw it downward while bringing fingers and thumb together; close the eyes slightly.

cards.front: How do you sign BED in ASL?
cards.back: Put the side of your head against joined palms as if resting on a pillow.

cards.front: How do you sign HOME in ASL?
cards.back: Touch gathered dominant fingertips near the mouth, then move them to the cheek near the ear.

cards.front: How do you sign HOUSE in ASL?
cards.back: Use two flat hands to outline a peaked roof with fingertips meeting, then move the hands apart and down to outline walls.
cards.example: Refer to a house as a building.

cards.front: How do you sign CAR in ASL?
cards.back: Hold two fists as if gripping a steering wheel and turn them slightly back and forth.

cards.front: How do you sign BICYCLE in ASL?
cards.back: Make two fists and rotate them in alternating forward circles, like pedals.

cards.front: How do you sign AIRPLANE in ASL?
cards.back: Extend the thumb, index finger, and little finger of the dominant hand; point forward and move the hand forward and slightly upward.
cards.example: Refer to an airplane or flight.

cards.front: How do you sign BATHROOM in ASL?
cards.back: Form a dominant T hand and shake it side to side. This also serves for TOILET.

cards.front: How do you sign DOOR in ASL?
cards.back: Hold two flat hands upright side by side, palms forward; swing one hand back like a hinged door.

cards.front: How do you sign WHITE in ASL?
cards.back: Place an open dominant hand on the upper chest, palm toward the body. Pull it outward while gathering the fingers and thumb together.

cards.front: How do you sign BLACK in ASL?
cards.back: Hold the dominant index finger horizontally near the forehead and draw it sideways across the forehead.

cards.front: How do you sign HOT in ASL?
cards.back: Hold a clawed or C-like dominant hand near the mouth and move it outward while turning the palm down, as if discarding something hot.

cards.front: How do you sign COLD in ASL?
cards.back: Hold fists near the sides of the chest and shake them slightly as if shivering.

cards.front: How do you sign RAIN in ASL?
cards.back: Hold both open hands palm down and lower them repeatedly while wiggling the fingers like falling drops.

cards.front: How do you sign SUN in ASL?
cards.back: Trace a small circle above and to the side of the head with the dominant index finger, then open the hand downward into rays.

cards.front: How do you sign TREE in ASL?
cards.back: Hold the dominant elbow on the back of the horizontal nondominant hand. Raise the dominant forearm with fingers spread and twist the raised hand slightly.

cards.front: How do you sign FLOWER in ASL?
cards.back: Bring gathered dominant fingertips near one side of the nose, then the other, as if smelling a flower.

cards.front: How do you sign CAT in ASL?
cards.back: Near each cheek, pull a thumb-index pinch outward as if tracing whiskers. A one-handed form also occurs.

cards.front: How do you sign BIRD in ASL?
cards.back: Near the mouth, open and close the dominant index finger against the thumb like a beak.

cards.front: How do you sign FISH in ASL?
cards.back: Hold a flat dominant hand sideways and move it forward with a gentle side-to-side wiggle, like a swimming fish.

cards.front: How do you sign RED in ASL?
cards.back: Brush the dominant index fingertip downward near the lips.

cards.front: How do you sign BLUE in ASL?
cards.back: Hold a dominant B hand outward and shake or twist it gently at the wrist.
